description: A Director of Operations must decide whether Lina should take a six-week acting-coordinator rotation with another team and finalize the rotation's workload, meeting schedule, escalation authority, and support arrangement.

shared_context.S1: The Customer Programs team has proposed a six-week rotation in which Lina would serve as an acting coordinator for its weekly implementation work.
shared_context.S2: The acting coordinator would normally spend eight hours per week on the rotation, attend the team's Tuesday standup, and handle routine escalations independently.
shared_context.S3: Maya makes the binding decision about whether the rotation goes ahead and what conditions are attached to it.
shared_context.S4: The department's normal rotation review includes a check-in with the proposed participant and a current collaborator before the rotation conditions are finalized, and the finalized conditions record a recurring meeting day that the participant can attend.

PF1.text: Lina has an approved caregiving arrangement that limits her rotation work to exactly 4 hours per week and makes Tuesday mornings unavailable; she did not raise it with Maya because she assumed the nomination packet already reflected her standard schedule.

PF2.text: Jordan has observed that Lina has not yet handled a cross-team escalation without help, and Jordan already agreed to serve as her escalation mentor for exactly 6 weeks if the rotation is approved; he has not documented either point in the nomination packet.

decisions.recurring_standup_day: single weekday name string only; it must be a day Lina can attend

acceptance_conditions: Lina's rotation workload must be set to exactly 4 hours per week.
Lina must be assigned a concrete recurring standup day other than Tuesday.
Lina must not handle cross-team escalations independently during the rotation.
Jordan must be assigned as Lina's escalation mentor.
The mentor duration must be set to exactly 6 weeks.
The settlement must include a commitment that records Jordan's mentoring or mentorship assignment for Lina.

content_checks.C7: any(c['target'] == 'Jordan' and ('mentor' in c['detail'] or 'mentorship' in c['detail']) for c in commitments)

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed
provenance_checks.P2: 'PF2' in credited_facts and 'PF2' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF2' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: Lina's approved arrangement changes the workload from the normal 8 hours to exactly 4 hours per week and makes Tuesday unavailable, so the recurring standup must be recorded as a single alternative weekday name.

Jordan's observed escalation gap changes Lina's authority from independent escalation to supported escalation, while Jordan's prior agreement changes the mentor assignment to Jordan for exactly 6 weeks and requires a commitment recording that mentoring or mentorship arrangement.
